text: World of Warcraft Classic is a 2019 massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed and published by Blizzard Entertainment, released globally on August 26, 2019. It runs alongside the main game and recreates World of Warcraft in its vanilla state, as it existed before the launch of the first expansion, The Burning Crusade, specifically at patch 1.12.1, around September 2006. The maximum character level is set to 60, all expansion content is absent, and nearly all original gameplay mechanics are preserved. Modern interface and functional enhancements from later expansions have been integrated, along with bug and exploit fixes from the original release. The game emphasizes social interaction, a feature many players felt was missing in more recent versions. Players can choose from the original eight races—humans, dwarves, gnomes, night elves (Alliance) and orcs, trolls, tauren, Forsaken (Horde)—and the original nine classes: druid, hunter, mage, paladin, priest, rogue, shaman, warlock, and warrior. Only Alliance players can become paladins, and only Horde players can become shamans; no expansion-added races or classes are available. The game world is restored to its pre-Cataclysm state, and expansion areas like Outland are inaccessible. Content was released in six phases to emulate the original patch cycle, with no changes to core game mechanics, which remain set to the 1.12.1 version. The demand for Classic and legacy realms grew significantly after Cataclysm made original content permanently inaccessible. Blizzard previously refused to create such servers, citing high development and support costs, and stated in 2008 that maintaining classic realms was not justified. Private servers, such as Nostalrius, emerged to replicate older versions, with Nostalrius reaching 800,000 registered accounts and 150,000 active players before shutting down in April 2016 due to a cease and desist letter. A Change.org petition with over 200,000 signatures was created and delivered to Blizzard leadership, prompting internal discussions. Blizzard acknowledged the community's interest and stated they had been considering legacy servers for years, though technical challenges delayed implementation. The Nostalrius team shared their source code with Valkyrie-WoW, and the servers returned as the Elysium Project on December 17, 2016. At BlizzCon 2017, J. Allen Brack announced Classic on stage, describing it as a faithful recreation of the original game on modern infrastructure. The game was developed by porting original 1.12.1 data and assets to modern servers and clients, allowing shared source code and access to performance and security improvements. In March 2020, Blizzard surveyed Classic players about a Burning Crusade version, which was confirmed in February 2021 and launched on June 1, 2021. In April 2022, Blizzard announced Wrath of the Lich King Classic, released on September 26, 2022. The developers aimed for minimal changes to preserve the original game feel, contrasting with Classic’s approach of preserving all original interactions. Both official and private servers traditionally used the end-patch state for each expansion. In Wrath of the Lich King Classic, the Dungeon Finder was excluded in favor of an improved bulletin board to promote social interaction. A limited-time 50% experience buff, Joyous Journeys, was introduced during the pre-patch and returned before each new content phase. Previously, players had to reach level 55 to unlock Death Knight, but this was changed to allow immediate creation, later reverted to prevent bot abuse. In the first phase, Naxxramas mob health and damage were increased due to original undertuning. In the second phase, Phase 1 bosses dropped 25-man difficulty items, and 10-man items were scattered in Heroic Dungeons via a new "Titan Rune Dungeon" difficulty, known as "Heroic+". All Ulduar bosses were released in their pre-nerf state, and gear on all difficulties had higher stats and item levels. Class balancing changes were introduced to improve performance and eliminate detrimental play styles. Cosmetic changes included full character recustomization, which was made available to all players in Classic, including gender (now called Body Type). Race and Faction Change features, introduced in the original Wrath of the Lich King, were added in Phase 2. The WoW Token, introduced during Warlords of Draenor, became available in Wrath of the Lich King Classic on May 23, 2023. Phase 3 launched on June 20, 2023, adding Argent Tournament, daily quests, Trial of the Champion, Trial of the Crusader and Grand Crusader raids, Onyxia's Lair, and Defense Protocol: Beta, a new dungeon difficulty. "Heroic" difficulty for raids was introduced immediately and could be toggled per boss, unlike the original 2008 release. Phase 4, released on October 10, 2023, added Icecrown Citadel, three Frozen Halls dungeons, Defense Protocol: Gamma, and introduced Random Dungeon Finder and Pets and Collections systems. Phase 5, released on January 11, 2024, added the Ruby Sanctum raid. At BlizzCon 2023, Blizzard announced that Wrath of the Lich King Classic would continue into Cataclysm content in the first half of 2024, with gameplay changes including continued use of the Titan Rune Dungeon system, faster leveling, and a faster content release. The 4.0 Cataclysm pre-patch launched on April 30, 2024, adding Worgen and Goblin races, new race/class combinations, and revamped 0-60 zones and quests. The expansion officially launched on May 20, 2024, unlocking level 80-85 zones and dungeons. The Rise of the Zandalari patch, released on July 30, 2024, introduced reimagined Zul'Gurub and Zul'Aman as 5-player dungeons for max-level characters. Content in the Rage of the Firelands patch became available on October 29, 2024, including the Firelands raid and "Elemental Rune Protocol: Inferno" dungeons, which allowed players to earn tokens for tier 11 raid items; the raid itself opened on November 6, 2024. The Hour of Twilight patch, released on February 18, 2025, added Dragon Soul, Hour of Twilight Dungeons, and "Elemental Rune Protocol: Twilight" difficulty, excluding Looking For Raid (LFR), which was instead accessible through Protocol: Twilight dungeons. In November 2024, during a 30th Anniversary livestream, Blizzard announced that Mists of Pandaria would launch in summer 2025. In April 2025, users began beta testing Mists of Pandaria Classic. The expansion launched on July 21, 2025, including original 85-90 quests, zones, dungeons, and raids, plus "Celestial Dungeons," modeled after the Elemental and Titan Rune dungeon systems from earlier expansions. Celestial Dungeons replaced the Raid Finder mode, which was not implemented. The first raid tier featured a staggered rollout of the three raid instances, with each raid's loot table integrated into the Celestial Dungeon system. In September 2025, Blizzard opened free character transfers to consolidate players onto "Mega Realms" in each region, citing benefits observed from prior transfers in Season of Discovery and Classic Era realms.

Mists of Pandaria Classic launched on July 21, 2025, offering the original 85-90 quests, zones, dungeons, and raids, along with new "Celestial Dungeons" modeled after the "Elemental Rune" and "Titan Rune" dungeon modes from Cataclysm Classic and Wrath of the Lich King Classic. These Celestial Dungeons were introduced as a replacement for the Raid Finder difficult mode, since Blizzard chose not to include Raid Finder in Mists of Pandaria Classic. The first raid tier featured a staggered rollout of the three raid instances, with each raid's loot table later integrated into the Celestial Dungeon system. In September 2025, Blizzard opened free character transfers to consolidate players onto "Mega Realms" in each region, based on observed benefits from prior transfers during Season of Discovery and Classic Era realms. On December 9, 2025, Phase 3 "The Thunder King" launched, adding the Isle of Thunder and Isle of Giants zones, the Throne of Thunder raid, and new story content centered on the Shado-Pan Assault faction and the continuation of the legendary questline; the Throne of Thunder raid opened two days later on December 11, 2025, marking the second-to-last raid in the Mists of Pandaria Expansion. During Warcraft Direct 2024, Blizzard announced a re-release of the 2004 version of World of Warcraft, launched on November 21, 2024, as the "20th Anniversary Edition," which retains most features from the 2019 Classic release and includes quality-of-life updates such as the Chronoboon Displacer, updated Honor System, removal of Buff and Debuff Limits, a native LFG tool, and a modern guild panel UI. Blizzard stated this edition would continue into The Burning Crusade starting in late 2025 or early 2026. On February 5, 2026, the 20th Anniversary Edition servers will transition into The Burning Crusade Classic. Hardcore-only servers were released with the 20th Anniversary Edition, featuring permadeath and an optional "Self-Found Mode," and Blizzard confirmed these servers will not progress to The Burning Crusade; characters can transfer to Normal realms to continue playing in The Burning Crusade Classic. Before Burning Crusade Classic launched, Blizzard created separate copies of each server known as Classic Era servers, while original realms automatically progressed with Burning Crusade content. Players could pay to create copies of their existing characters on Classic Era servers, which remained in a 1.12.1 state with all content phases unlocked, or freely create new characters to replay content in that state. Reinvented versions of World of Warcraft Classic have launched as separate servers to provide players with a fresh experience. Blizzard began seasonal Classic servers in November 2021 with Season of Mastery, which introduced more challenging mechanics and an "ironman" mode allowing players to progress without letting their characters die; Season of Mastery concluded on February 14, 2023. On August 24, 2023, official Hardcore Classic servers launched, featuring permadeath and the "Mak'gora" duel-to-death mode, inspired by community-created permadeath experiences using addons with restrictions like auction house access or trading; characters that die on Hardcore servers cannot log back in or resurrect but can transfer to Classic Era realms. On February 29, 2024, Self-Found Mode was added to Hardcore servers, preventing auction house use and mail sending/receiving, available only for new characters during creation and not reversible once disabled. On November 30, 2023, Season of Discovery launched as a seasonal server with new content in the base "Vanilla" world, including runes for class abilities and updated professions, featuring gated leveling (level 25 in Phase 1, incrementally increasing) and forced faction balance that locked players from creating a new character of the dominant faction. Each phase included reworked PvE and PvP content, such as a 10-player Blackfathom Deeps raid and a world PvP event in Ashenvale, and Blizzard tested anti-RMT measures like restricting new accounts from trading, sending mail, or using the auction house for 30 days. Phase 2 raised the level cap to 40, converted Gnomeregan into a 10-player raid, added a PvP event in Stranglethorn Vale called The Blood Moon, and introduced restrictions on GDKP runs. Phase 3 raised the level cap to 50, converted the Temple of Atal'Hakkar ("Sunken Temple") into a 20-player raid, and introduced persistent world events called Nightmare Incursions for reputation and rewards. Phase 4 increased the level cap to 60, added a new 5-player dungeon, Demon Fall Canyon, and unlocked a reworked Molten Core (20-player) and a reworked 40-man Onyxia's Lair. Phase 5 introduced updated versions of Zul'Gurub and Blackwing Lair raids, the new raid Crystal Vale, and a new boss in Demon Fall Canyon. Phase 6 added the "48-Hour War" event leading to the opening of the Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj and Temple of Ahn'Qiraj raids, with Ruins retuned for 10+ players and Temple changed to 20+ players, and the emerald dragons of Emeriss, Ysondre, Lethon, and Taerar moved into a special "Nightmare Grove" raid. Phase 7 introduced Naxxramas and the Scourge Invasion event, along with the Karazhan Crypts, a new 5-player dungeon in Deadwind Pass with new quests and items, originally planned as the final full patch but expanded due to community feedback. Phase 8 introduced the first all-new raid, Scarlet Enclave, added New Avalon—the first new zone in the Classic world—with new quests and supporting content, and marked the final content addition to Season of Discovery. PC Gamer scored Classic 80 out of 100, calling it a window into a time when online interactions felt novel and exciting, while Polygon praised its difficulty and design for fostering social connections, calling it a "faithful snapshot of a moment in time." Since launch, Blizzard has faced criticism for using layering technology to split communities and exploit the in-game economy, though as of October 10, 2019, most realms operate on a single layer, with only high-population servers still using multiple layers. The game won "PC Game of the Year" at the 2019 Golden Joystick Awards and was nominated for "Game, Classic Revival" at the NAVGTR Awards.
